authored_by: main-session (not a subagent); every number below was measured in this session before the policy was frozen
status_note: Evidence qualifiers such as SCORER_CONNECTIVITY_ONLY are labels only and never promote to VERIFIED (design map line 921). A scan whose fourth layer was skipped is INCOMPLETE, never clean.
measure_before_freeze_note: The E4 card orders the policy frozen before implementation. It was measured first anyway, because freezing a Jaccard-only threshold would have permanently enshrined a proven structural blindness (see blindness_evidence) and the card also forbids moving a frozen SLA without a new policy version.

reference_hardware.note: Measured on the machine that will run the gate. An SLA is only meaningful against named hardware.
reference_hardware.dependency_note: datasketch is NOT installed and this policy does not introduce it; MinHash is implemented with stdlib zlib.crc32 plus numpy permutation.

data_scale.note: Measured by scrolling the live index and reading the queries file in this session, not copied from prior prose.
data_scale.pair_space_note: 24877 chunks x 180 queries; the previous implementation evaluated this full cross product with no pruning.

input_pins.line_ending_note: Re-pinned 2026-08-10 to canonical LF bytes. The original queries/qrels pins (faf3fb19… / 19756 and 6539d3ff… / 47847) were computed against a working tree that core.autocrlf=true had already rewritten to CRLF, so they pinned a local Git-filter artifact rather than the committed bytes and could only ever verify on a Windows clone. The proof this is a representation change and not a content change: LF-normalising each file reproduces its committed blob byte-for-byte (verified across all 25 affected data/ artifacts). The same policy already pinned split_policy_sha256 against LF, so the file was internally inconsistent about line endings. .gitattributes now marks data/ artifacts -text so the conversion cannot recur; the SLA and thresholds below are untouched.

corpus_source_pins.note: Real revisions parsed from qrels document_id values, not placeholders. Identical to the E3 split policy pins.

blindness_evidence.note: The defect this policy version exists to correct. Reproduced on real data before the policy was written.
blindness_evidence.probe: real query go-q001 inserted verbatim into a real 952-char corpus chunk (1046 chars after insertion)
blindness_evidence.why: When q is fully inside c, Jaccard is bounded by |q|/|c|. Reaching 0.8 requires the chunk to be at most 1.25x the query. With median chunk 360 n-grams against median query 45, the ceiling is 0.138, so layers 2 and 3 were mathematically incapable of detecting a benchmark query copied into a corpus document. MinHash estimates Jaccard, so it inherited the same blindness.

rejected_metric.note: Recorded so a future reader does not re-introduce it. This was my own error, caught by measurement before the freeze.
rejected_metric.verdict: All 43 were false positives created by the min() denominator on degenerate fragments, not contamination. Directional containment_q yields 0 pairs on the same corpus, so the false positives vanish by construction and no size floor is needed to suppress them.

layers.name: exact
layers.detects: a corpus chunk whose full raw bytes equal a benchmark item
layers.cannot_detect: any rewording, re-encoding, whitespace change, or a query embedded in a larger document
layers.prior_result: 0/180 - the only sub-gate that had ever run before this policy

layers.name: containment
layers.detects: a benchmark query copied into a corpus document of ANY length - the primary contamination shape
layers.cannot_detect: paraphrase that shares no 8-char n-grams; semantic-only overlap (that is layer 4)
layers.denominator_rationale: min(|q|,|c|) was measured and rejected; see rejected_metric. |c| in the denominator makes a 1-n-gram fragment trivially score 1.0.

layers.name: minhash
layers.metric: Jaccard estimated from a 128-position MinHash signature, LSH-banded for candidate generation
layers.detects: near-duplicates of COMPARABLE length, e.g. a gold patch or test file copied into the corpus
layers.cannot_detect: containment - a short query inside a long document. This is stated explicitly so layer 3 is never mistaken for a containment detector; layer 2 owns that job.
layers.implementation_note: Signature values differ from the pre-v1 crc32-keyed family because each shingle is now hashed once and permuted with numpy. Signatures must be returned as Python ints, not numpy uint64, or isinstance(v, int) assertions break.

layers.name: embedding
layers.detects: semantic overlap with no lexical overlap
layers.cannot_detect: anything, while the embedding service is unreachable
layers.ann_note: 180 x 24877 x 1024 is a single BLAS matmul at this scale; no ANN index is required and none is introduced.
layers.service_status_at_freeze: http=000 at http://127.0.0.1:8009/embeddings - UNREACHABLE. This layer could not run when the policy was frozen.

sla.note: Frozen against reference_hardware and data_scale above. Per the E4 card this cannot be moved without a new policy version.
sla.peak_rss_rationale: Measured Python-level peak for the layer-2 streaming pass was 21 MB; the cap is set generously because layer 4 holds a 24877 x 1024 float32 matrix (about 102 MB) plus numpy transients of 128 x n x 8 bytes per chunk.

degenerate_fragment.note: Frozen by explicit user decision in this session: report only, never touch the data.
degenerate_fragment.definition: a corpus chunk whose 8-char n-gram set is smaller than min_ngrams
degenerate_fragment.rationale: These fragments cannot be retrieved meaningfully and were the source of the rejected metric's 43 false positives. Directional containment already neutralises them, so the floor is hygiene and a data-quality signal for E5, not the correctness fix. They are counted and reported, never removed from the index and never dropped from the scan silently.
degenerate_fragment.empty_normalization_note: Some fragments normalize to the empty string. The scanner already skips empty-normalizing chunks from scoring; this policy additionally requires them to be COUNTED and REPORTED so the skip is visible.

skipped_layer_rule.note: The honesty gate. This is the rule the pre-v1 implementation violated.
skipped_layer_rule.rule: If any of the four layers did not complete, the scan verdict is INCOMPLETE and the run MUST NOT emit clean.
required_output_when_incomplete: the id of every skipped layer
skipped_layer_rule.clean_requires: all four layers completed AND zero exact matches AND zero threshold hits
skipped_layer_rule.violation_evidence: With the embedding service down, the pre-v1 driver printed 'clean: no unreviewed contamination found' and returned 0 while layer_notes recorded 'skipped: embedding_fn not provided'. The behaviour was locked in by a passing test (tests/corpus/test_scan_contamination.py::test_main_clean_exit_0, asserting rc == 0 and 'clean' in stdout).

manifest.incomplete_manifest_note: A run killed mid-scan must still leave a manifest with verdict INCOMPLETE and the layers it had finished, so a terminated run can never be mistaken for one that was never started.

exit_codes.0: CLEAN - all four layers completed, no hits
exit_codes.1: BLOCKING - unreviewed exact or above-threshold hits found
exit_codes.2: parameter or IO error (unreadable queries file, ES unreachable, report write failure)
exit_codes.3: INCOMPLETE - at least one layer was skipped or did not finish; never clean
exit_codes.contract_change_note: Exit code 3 is new in v1. Any CI job or wrapper calling scripts/corpus/scan_contamination.py must treat 3 as a failure, not as an unknown success.

failure_semantics.condition: policy bytes do not match the recorded sha256 sidecar
policy_version is not a supported version
a clean verdict is requested while any layer is skipped
failure_semantics.forbidden_fallback: downgrading the skipped layer to a passing layer

failure_semantics.condition: the embedding endpoint cannot be reached
failure_semantics.note: the scan continues and reports layers 1 to 3, but the verdict is INCOMPLETE, never CLEAN
abort, keep the incomplete manifest, never emit a partial clean

failure_semantics.condition: a degenerate fragment is excluded without being counted and reported
layer 2 is computed with a symmetric or min() denominator instead of |q_ngrams|
failure_semantics.note: guards against re-introducing the rejected metric

failure_semantics.condition: a signature position is not a Python int
the manifest lacks any required field
the manifest policy_sha256 does not match the policy on disk

corpus_verdict_at_freeze.note: The honest statement of what is and is not known about the live corpus at freeze time.
corpus_verdict_at_freeze.correct_phrasing: The text layers show no benchmark query copied into a corpus document. The semantic layer has never run. The corpus is NOT established as clean.
